question: Which of the following is an external agency with which NABARD has collaborated to promote micro - finance in 2005 - 06 ?

options.text: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development

solution:
The correct answer is __**Swiss Agency for Development Cooperation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) is an international cooperation agency within the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA).
 
• It is responsible for the overall coordination of development activities and humanitarian aid delivered by the Swiss Confederation.
 
• In 2005-06, NABARD collaborated with SDC to promote micro-finance in India, aiming to improve the financial inclusion of the rural poor.
 
• SDC has a long-standing history of supporting various development projects across the globe, with a focus on poverty reduction, sustainable development, and economic cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)**

 
 
• Established on 12 July 1982, NABARD is an apex development bank in India.
 
• Its mandate is to promote sustainable and equitable agriculture and rural development through participative financial and non-financial interventions, innovations, technology, and institutional development for securing prosperity.
 
• NABARD provides refinance support for building rural infrastructure and strengthening rural credit delivery systems, besides other activities.
 
 
 
• **Micro-finance**
 
 
• Micro-finance refers to financial services, such as loans, savings, insurance, and fund transfers, provided to low-income individuals or groups who traditionally lack access to banking services.
 
• It is designed to promote financial inclusion and support entrepreneurship, reduce poverty, and empower economically disadvantaged communities.
 
• Micro-finance institutions (MFIs) play a crucial role in providing these services to the underserved sections of society.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**
 
 
• Established in 1944, the IMF is an organization of 190 countries working to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, facilitate international trade, promote high employment and sustainable economic growth, and reduce poverty around the world.
 
• The IMF provides policy advice, financial assistance, and technical assistance to its member countries.
 
 
 
• **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)**
 
 
• Also known as the World Bank, the IBRD is an international financial institution that offers loans and financial assistance to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries for development projects.
 
• Its goal is to reduce poverty and support sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **New Development Bank (NDB)**
 
 
• Established by the BRICS states (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa) in 2014, the NDB supports public or private projects through loans, guarantees, equity participation, and other financial instruments.
 
• Its primary focus is on infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS and other emerging economies and developing countries.
